answer: Every closed taxonomy class (severed-stream, adapter-exit-n, win-arg-limit, timeout, schema-invalid, partial-artifact, degraded, blocked) was induced, classified from symptoms, and formatted into WHAT/WHY/NEXT; each scored 3/3. A bare traceback and the shrug 'Operation failed.' scored 0. The naive always-3 scorer still awards 3 to the traceback, so the rubric is not a constant. SUCCESS:TST-0244

question: Does every class in the failure taxonomy produce a message that names what failed, why, and the exact next command? PASS requires full taxonomy coverage; a bare stack trace or an error with no next action is FAIL.

reviewer.method: Independent probe scores a live traceback at 0 and a catalog timeout message at 3; a constant-3 naive scorer fails the control.

title: Every failure class emits an actionable message (what, why, next command)
